original_question: Let G be a finite soluble group with triality, which means that G admits a group of automorphisms S isomorphic to the symmetric group of degree 3 given by the presentation S = ⟨σ, ρ | σ 2 = ρ3 = 1; σρσ = ρ2 ⟩ such that m · mρ · mρ = 1 for all m in the set of commutators M(G):= {[g, σ] | g ∈ G}. Suppose in addition that G = [G, S], the group G is generated by d elements of M(G) and their images under S, and xn = 1 for all x ∈ M(G). Is it true that the Fitting height of G is bounded in terms of d and n? An affirmative answer would provide a reduction of the analogue of the Restricted Burnside Problem for Moufang loops to the nilpotent case.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.54 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": the open problem asking whether the Fitting height of a finite soluble group with triality is bounded in terms of d and n under the stated generation and exponent hypotheses.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches Problem 21.54 very closely. It correctly identifies the setting of finite soluble groups with triality, the automorphism group S isomorphic to S_3 with presentation <sigma, rho | sigma^2 = rho^3 = 1, sigma rho sigma = rho^2>, the notation M(G) = {[g, sigma] | g in G}, the extra assumptions G = [G, S], generation by d elements from M(G) together with their S-images, the exponent condition x^n = 1 for all x in M(G), the conclusion sought (a bound for the Fitting height in terms of d and n), and the intended motivation from the Moufang-loop analogue of the Restricted Burnside Problem.
missing_details: The triality identity should read m · m^rho · m^(rho^2) = 1 for all m in M(G); the draft drops the exponent 2 on the last rho.
To make the question fully stand-alone, define [g, sigma] = g^{-1} g^sigma and [G, S] = <[g, s] : g in G, s in S>.
The generation hypothesis should be made explicit as: there exist m_1, ..., m_d in M(G) such that G = <m_i^s : 1 <= i <= d, s in S>.
It is worth stating that M(G) is a set of commutators and is not assumed to be a subgroup.
Replace the phrase 'bounded in terms of d and n' by the explicit existence of a function f(d, n) with h(G) <= f(d, n), where h(G) denotes the Fitting height.
State explicitly that d and n are positive integers.
refined_question: Let G be a finite soluble group, and let S = <sigma, rho | sigma^2 = rho^3 = 1, sigma rho sigma = rho^2> <= Aut(G), so that S is isomorphic to S_3. Assume that G is a group with triality, meaning that for M(G) := {[g, sigma] = g^{-1} g^sigma | g in G} one has m · m^rho · m^(rho^2) = 1 for every m in M(G). Suppose moreover that G = [G, S], and that there exist elements m_1, ..., m_d in M(G) such that G = <m_i^s : 1 <= i <= d, s in S>, and that x^n = 1 for all x in M(G). Must there exist a function f(d, n) such that the Fitting height h(G) satisfies h(G) <= f(d, n)?
justification: The nearest official formulation in the paper is Problem 21.54, and your draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of it. The only substantive correction needed is the triality identity, which in the paper is m · m^rho · m^(rho^2) = 1. The rewrite keeps the scope exactly where the paper places it: finite soluble groups with triality, with the same auxiliary hypotheses and the same Moufang-loop motivation, while making the implicit notation [g, sigma], [G, S], and the generation condition fully explicit.
